bugs.name: Wiki search does not return a page for its exact title
bugs.summary: Searching the fresh wiki page by its exact title persistently returned “No results”; searching its exact body phrase eventually returned the page, so the reported body-text failure was not reproduced.
bugs.expected: Searching the visible Search wiki field for the exact title of an existing wiki page should return that page. The field presents itself as a wiki-wide search, and the query is the exact title of a visible page, not an unrelated or ambiguous term.
bugs.actual: For the newly saved page MOExplore-4f7c91-WikiSearch, the exact-title query left the search popover at “No results” for at least 35 seconds, including on a repeat after re-focusing the field. The page title and body remained visible. The exact body phrase did eventually return the page after about 20 seconds, so the report's claim that both queries persistently fail was not confirmed.
reproSteps: Using the supplied signed-in repository-owner session (the page activity is attributed in the UI to “QA Profile Fixture”; no interactive sign-in or credential environment variables were used), open /momentic-admin/field-notes/wiki.

Create a new wiki page titled MOExplore-4f7c91-WikiSearch with body text “MOExplore searchable content phrase,” then save it. Do not use or edit the other listed wiki pages. The saved page is visible at /momentic-admin/field-notes/wiki/MOExplore-4f7c91-WikiSearch.-.

In the Search wiki field, enter the exact title MOExplore-4f7c91-WikiSearch. The popover settles on “No results” and remains there for at least 35 seconds while the matching page title and body remain visible. Clicking the magnifying-glass icon dismisses the popover without navigating.

As a falsification check, replace the query with the exact body phrase “MOExplore searchable content phrase.” After approximately 20 seconds, the popover returns the newly created page with that body snippet. Re-enter the exact title and re-focus the field; “No results” appears again.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected the reported expectation as inconsistent with intended behavior. The feature was shipped as Basic wiki content search using git-grep, with a release note explicitly describing matched files and content matches. Its pinned TestWikiSearchContent requests a body word and checks resulting page titles. A later UI fix ensures results display page titles rather than filenames; that is presentation, not an extension of the searched fields. Therefore a title absent from the page body has no required match under the shipped content-search contract. The candidate borrows a broader title-search expectation from the generic Search wiki placeholder. Any separately alleged response latency remains outside this intent conclusion.
